articles.title: Show HN: HeyCube – The personalized feed for your always-on AI agents
articles.content: Hi HN, I'm Fengli, founder of Inxpanse. HeyCube is our first product: the personalized feed for your always-on AI agents.While building my own always-on agents, I kept watching the token and search API costs add up really fast. Then I noticed the scheduled tasks in ChatGPT/Grok Bot/etc. also use up a lot of your plan's allowance, often on checks that find nothing new. That's why many people still don't leave their agents truly always on.This reminded me of the eras we humans have been through too: first search engines, then feeds. So I thought, why not build agents a feed of their own? That's why we built HeyCube. It reads sources around the clock and sends what fits you to the right agent, so your tokens go to the work itself. It's free and live at heycube.ai now, and works with ChatGPT, Grok Bot, Muse, Claude Code, and other agents in beta.I'm looking forward to you giving your agents a feed and seeing what they can do. Let me know if you have any questions/comments/feature requests

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 26 日消息，由《碧蓝航线》开发商蛮啾网络打造的幻想大世界 RPG《蓝色星原：旅谣》将于 11 月 26 日 10:00 正式开启公测，登陆 PC、iOS、安卓、鸿蒙与 PS5 平台。该作由上海蛮啾网络科技有限公司研发并运营，采用 Unity 引擎开发，背景音乐有川井宪次、西木康智等作曲家参与。海外发行方面，日服由蛮啾网络与悠星联合发行，韩服由 NEXON 代理，东南亚地区由 PlayPark 负责。故事舞台为幻想大陆普罗米利亚。玩家扮演“星临者”重返这片土地，在灾变后秩序失衡的世界中游历，追寻散落于天地间的星光传说。与常见的开放世界产品不同，本作不设强制线性流程，探索解谜、动作战斗与家园经营之间的切换由玩家自行安排。核心玩法围绕幻想生物“奇波”展开（IT之家注：奇波为本作中对幻想生物的统称）。目前游戏内已实装两百余种奇波，不同物种拥有各自的生态习性与地域亚种。奇波可上场参战并释放技能，也能化为飞行、水上骑乘载具，用于跨越地形或破解环境机关，还可派驻家园牧场承担种植、采集与生产。官方信息显示，游戏全球预约量已突破 2500 万，预约里程碑奖励包含常驻角色“艾妮丝”、限定奇波“星彩 · 浮云”等。在此前的“旅迹测试”中，开发组重做了奇波对战机制与捕捉动画，取消捕捉时的强制暂停，并对家园经营与养成线做了减负调整。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 25 日消息，奕境汽车品牌总经理曾清林刚刚发文，分享了 70% 和 90% 两组数据：70% 来自工信部。2026 年以来，搭载辅助驾驶功能的乘用车新车，市场渗透率已经达到 70%。这再次印证，新能源上半场是电动化，现在来到了下半场的智能化。随着充电网络的普及和续航的提升，充电和续航对很多朋友来说已经不再是主要焦虑，真正的考题在智驾。90% 这个数据来自华为智能辅助驾驶后台：买了华为智驾车型的车主，90% 以上每天都在用。这个数据在我身上也可以得到验证。我目前开奕境 X9，每天 90% 的路程都是智驾开的。曾清林表示，有的智能辅助驾驶，让用户雨天不敢用、晚上没法用，极端工况更是害怕用，这样的智驾只会给用户添麻烦。问题往往出在感知硬件上。摄像头在夜晚、雨天、小目标面前存在短板，硬件看不全、看不准，算法再强也无从判断。他认为，要补上这些短板，激光雷达的数量和布局，就是绕不过去的一环。四激光，正是面向 L3、一步到位的智驾硬件方案。曾清林透露，即将亮相华为乾崑生态大会的奕境 X9 纯电版在这方面准备了惊喜。预计新车会采用四激光方案。据IT之家此前报道，奕境 X9 于 9 月 24 日上市，限时优惠价 27.98 万-35.98 万元，号称满配华为乾崑全栈智能，拥有华为乾崑智驾、鸿蒙座舱、华为乾崑赤兔平台、华为乾崑车载光、华为乾崑车云、华为鲸鳍通信加持。此外，奕境 X9 纯电版车型将于 11 月 27 日上市，该车将搭载超带宽千伏平台，号称“充电更快更从容”。

articles.title: 北京汽车 T700 新车申报：1.5T 增程动力、单 / 双电机两种版本
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 25 日消息，工信部发布第 414 批《道路机动车辆生产企业及产品公告》新产品公示，北汽 T700 完成申报。本次申报的车型由北京汽车集团越野车有限公司生产，隶属于北京牌，定位为插电式增程混合动力运动型乘用车，车尾分别标注“T700”与“北汽集团”字样。根据外观及动力差异，公示中包含两种版本，整体造型延续方正硬派的方盒子设计语言，配备贯穿式尾灯与银色下护板装饰。IT之家注意到，两种版本的三围尺寸均为长 4973mm、宽 2019mm，轴距同为 3050mm ，额定载客 5 人。基础版本高度为 1930mm，整备质量 2410kg，最高车速 180km/h；高配版本高度略降为 1910mm，整备质量提升至 2700kg，最高车速达到 200km/h，同时可选装牵引专用装置（电连接头、拖钩孔），准拖挂车总质量最高 2000kg。动力方面，两款车型均搭载由北京汽车动力总成有限公司生产的 A156T3 型 1.5T 增程器，排量 1498ml，发动机额定功率 115kW、最大净功率 110kW，满足国 Ⅵ 排放要求。区别在于：基础版采用单电机后驱布局，驱动电机峰值功率 200kW，储能装置为蜂巢能源科技（盐城）有限公司供应的磷酸铁锂蓄电池；高配版升级为前后双电机四驱，前电机峰值功率 165kW、后电机峰值功率 200kW，储能装置更换为蜂巢能源科技股份有限公司供应的三元锂离子蓄电池。此外，两款车型均允许外接充电，配备 EDR 汽车事件数据记录系统，可选装 ETC 车载装置与不同样式轮辋，轮胎规格提供 255/60R20 与 275/45R22 两种选择，ABS 系统由博世汽车部件（苏州）有限公司提供。以下为汽车参数详情：▲ 磷酸铁锂单电机版▲ 三元锂双电机牵引版

articles.title: “独立”微信音乐悄悄上线：内置在听一听中，曲库来源于 QQ 音乐
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 25 日消息，据公众号“大厂产品”分享，微信也有了自己的音乐产品。打开微信发现页中的听一听，进入「我的-个人歌单」会看到个人歌单下显示有微信音乐。虽然是微信音乐，但歌曲还是来源于 QQ 音乐。除了微信音乐外，用户还可绑定 QQ 音乐、酷狗音乐。QQ 音乐是使用微信账号，绑定 QQ 音乐账号后，同步 QQ 音乐收藏、最近播放歌曲。酷狗音乐也和 QQ 音乐类似，是和微信账号绑定和同步的操作。从目前的分享来看，微信音乐内置在听一听中，是听一听的一部分，其曲库来源于 QQ 音乐，不过有微信音乐自己的推荐、评论、分享、共享等玩法。大家在IT之家微信号回复“微信”两字，即可获取当前最新官方内部版微信下载。

articles.title: 踩刹车！李想宣布理想汽车更新节奏从一年一次调整为两年一次
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 25 日消息，据理想车友群分享，在理想汽车 2026 年第三季度财报电话会上，理想汽车董事长兼 CEO 李想透露，理想车型的更新节奏会从过去的一年一次调整为两年左右一次。理想汽车认为这个调整对于用户、行业、供应商和自己都是更有利的。首先，它符合工信部两冬一夏的测试验证要求。这样的验证要求对于车的质量、车的验证以及行业的健康度，我认为是非常有利的。所以我们要坚定地执行。第二，这个节奏对用户会更友好。更长的产品周期意味着更好的保值率，更稳定的产品服务，还有更好的体验，包括软件的迭代也都会变得更好，能够给用户带来更高的满意度。第三，我们今年完成了自研的三电和芯片的搭载。整个核心的自研能够让我们更有效地控制技术和技术平台，而不是被电池和芯片厂商的节奏带着走。所以对我们更广泛的供应商来说，更稳定的这种更新节奏、更长的周期，也能让产能的规划和质量都变得更好。IT之家注意到，李想称，2027 年会补充一到两个单独的车型，不会做大面积的改款。这个是理想汽车的一个核心的规划。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 25 日现场消息，在今天下午的 HarmonyOS 创新技术沟通会上，华为 Fellow、HarmonyOS 首席架构师李世军分享了鸿蒙在互联方面的探索。据李世军介绍，个人的手机、平板、电脑、穿戴设备越来越多，设备间的自然、无缝、稳定连接变得越来越重要，而连接环境复杂，有蓝牙、Wi-Fi、NFC 等。华为通过鸿蒙分布式软总线，让复杂的、分散的无线技术收拢成了有序的横向网络，设备连接更简单方便。李世军表示，过去分布式主要聚焦鸿蒙 HarmonyOS 设备，而现在进一步升级为鸿蒙星河互联。IT之家在沟通会现场了解到，鸿蒙星河互联现在不仅可以连 HarmonyOS 设备，而且可以连接更多的 OpenHarmony 生态设备，同时开放跨 OS 的互通能力，连接更多跨系统的设备。

articles.title: 态度反转：消息称亚马逊与 Meta 洽谈合作，或将开放商城给 Muse AI 购物助手
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 25 日消息，有消息显示，亚马逊对 Meta 旗下 AI 智能体 Muse 的态度或许正在转变。两大巨头正在洽谈一项合作，希望让 Muse 直接接入亚马逊电商平台。IT之家注意到，这次谈判和两个月前的局面形成鲜明反差：当时用户尝试通过 Muse 在亚马逊下单结账时，会直接收到报错，亚马逊对 Muse 实施了屏蔽。《财富》当地时间周三援引知情人士报道，双方已经开展多轮磋商。目前谈判卡在两个核心议题：合作模式下商品搜索结果如何展示、广告业务怎么安排。亚马逊最大的顾虑，是 Muse 这类第三方购物智能体会冲击自身广告收入。今年 10 月，亚马逊 CEO 安迪 · 贾西还表态，通过外部 AI 智能体下单的用户规模并不大。另一个考量是，亚马逊可能打算等 Muse 产品更加成熟之后再开放接入。如果 Muse 下错订单、交易出问题，最终需要亚马逊去安抚不满的消费者和卖家。知情人士称，亚马逊高管还担心，第三方 AI 购物智能体会削弱亚马逊直接触达用户、维系消费者关系的能力。报道同时提到，这份潜在合作协议，最终需要两家公司 CEO 批准才能落地。

articles.title: 古尔曼：苹果内部已测试 iPad 运行 macOS，但暂无面向消费者落地计划
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 25 日消息，iPad 早已用上和 Mac 同源的 Apple Silicon 芯片，很多用户都希望苹果能允许直接在平板上运行 macOS，摆脱目前 iPadOS 不够顺手的窗口管理。而触屏版 MacBook Pro 的推出，也让苹果过去“不做设备融合”的说辞说服力下降。彭博社马克 · 古尔曼在播客问答中透露，苹果内部确实已经实现 iPad 运行 macOS，但大家不必期待它很快对外发布。IT之家注意到，随着 iPad 硬件性能持续变强，配套系统功能追赶得比较吃力：iPadOS 26 才正式加入完整窗口功能，但这套界面相比 macOS 依旧生硬，这也是很多用户期盼 macOS 登陆 iPad 的原因。古尔曼表示：苹果内部很早就有可以跑 macOS 的 iPad 样机，得益于 iPad 与 Mac 统一的 Apple Silicon 底层架构，技术上具备测试条件。不过他核实后确认，目前没有立项把 macOS 改造为面向普通消费者、可以在 iPad 上公开使用的版本，短期不会落地。苹果的路线依旧是持续零散迭代 iPadOS，一点点补齐功能、拉近和 Mac 的能力差距，而不是两套系统完全合并。同时，传闻已久的超大折叠 iPad 项目（代号 Project J312）还在开发。古尔曼对这款产品很看好：它是 19 至 20 英寸的折叠 iPad，形态类似放大版的 iPhone Duo，外屏位置没有副屏。但该项目不确定性很高：原定时间从 2027–2028 推迟到了 2029 年，成本、良率问题随时可能让项目直接被砍掉。如果最终能够上市，定价预计在 3,000 到 5,000 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 20,035 到 33,391 元人民币）区间。

articles.title: 从 AGI 到 ASI，DeepMind 提出让 AI 自己「开公司」、重塑组织架构，自己进化
articles.content: 100 个 AI 联合做题竟学会「集体作弊」？谷歌抛出 ASI 演进新框架，揭示组织化进化的恐怖与隐忧。    作者丨郑佳美    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       刚刚，Google DeepMind 抛出了一套从 AGI 迈向 ASI 的技术演进框架，其中有个相当大胆的设想：未来 AI 的能力增长，可能要靠它自己学会组建公司，甚至不断重写公司的组织架构。这套框架提出了 Cooperative RSI（合作式递归自我改进）机制。设想一下，成千上万个 AI Agent 可以自行分工、积累专业经验、调整协作关系，再把节省下来的算力投入新一轮研发。随着组织效率提高，系统又获得更多资源来改造自身，形成持续迭代的增长循环。这意味着，未来 AI 的进化单位可能从单个模型扩展为整个研发组织，连任务分配、专业分工和知识传递机制也会成为可优化的技术变量。不过，增加 Agent 容易，让一个组织持续创造超出资源消耗的能力增益却困难得多。Cooperative RSI 究竟怎样形成递归增长，组织效率能否像模型能力一样被规模化扩展，以及谁来判断 AI 对自身的改造确实有效？ 这些问题构成了这套框架中颇有研究空间的技术核心。01从模型扩展到组织扩展过去，AI 能力增长主要依赖模型架构、训练数据和计算规模。当多个 Agent 开始共同承担复杂研发任务时，计算资源与能力之间的关系就没有那么直接了。问题出在任务依赖和协调成本上。复杂研发通常包含大量相互依赖的环节，上游结果决定下游工作能否继续。增加 Agent 可以提高独立任务的并行吞吐，却无法直接缩短任务依赖图中的关键路径。随着成员规模扩大，中间结果传递、上下文同步和冲突解决还会消耗额外资源，组织甚至可能因为协调开销过高而降低整体效率。这使 Multi-Agent Scaling Laws 与传统模型扩展规律出现明显差异。模型扩展主要考察计算投入与性能之间的关系，而组织扩展还必须考虑通信拓扑、任务可拆分程度、成员能力差异以及知识复用效率。DeepMind 强调了数字智能区别于人类组织的几个特征：Agent 可以复制运行状态，通过高带宽通道共享知识，并在不同计算节点之间迁移工作。这些条件降低了知识传播和协作重组的成本，但复制相同模型也会带来高度相关的推理偏差。即使不同 Agent 承担不同角色，共同的知识盲区仍可能让错误在组织内部相互强化。因此，专业化需要深入到系统架构中。不同 Agent 可以维护独立的长期记忆、专用工具、领域知识和验证流程，使特定类型的工作逐渐形成可复用的执行能力。随着经验积累，部分重复推理可以转化为程序调用，原本反复生成的中间结果也能够被稳定继承。雷峰网这种变化产生了两种不同的扩展收益。并行化改善任务完成时间，专业化则可能降低单位成果消耗的计算资源。后者还有一个额外特征：积累的工具与知识可以跨越多轮任务继续发挥作用。不过，专业岗位本身存在运行和维护成本，分工越细，跨角色协调也可能越复杂。因此，组织需要根据任务频率、知识复用程度与协作开销动态调整结构，避免专业化反过来拖累研发效率。当专业化能够持续产生超过维护成本的资源盈余时，组织便具备了进一步扩张的条件。而 Cooperative RSI 试图利用的，正是这部分可以重新投入研发的资源。02组织如何形成递归增长？DeepMind 将 AI 的递归自我改进划分为 Genetic RSI、Memetic RSI 和 Cooperative RSI。三者对应不同的优化对象：Genetic RSI 改进模型、算法与系统设计，Memetic RSI 积累程序、知识和可复用的研究成果，Cooperative RSI 则进一步调整创造这些成果的组织结构。它的底层逻辑与经济学中的专业分工有相似之处。当某类工作形成稳定需求，建立专门岗位所需的固定成本便有机会被大量任务摊薄。专业角色积累的知识与工具可以降

articles.title: OpenAI 联手 AMD，在旗舰 GPU 中抠出 14% 物理极限
articles.content: 不到 5 个月完成约 1 年工程进展，从自研推理芯片 Jalapeño 到商用流片，大模型正式接管前端微架构。    作者丨郑佳美    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       刚刚，OpenAI 让 AI 直接改写的芯片电路，进入了 AMD 的实际制造流程。而且，改的还是已经被工程师打磨多年的旗舰 GPU IP。要知道，在芯片设计领域，有一条不成文的铁律：越接近商业量产的成熟旗舰 IP，优化的边际成本就越高。全球顶尖芯片架构师与物理设计团队历时数年、耗费数千万美元打磨出的电路，往往到了迭代后期，连 1% 到 2% 的性能功耗面积（PPA）提升都要付出极高的工程代价。现在，模型直接修改 SystemVerilog RTL，在既有设计上取得幅度达 14% 的 PPA 改进，这已经不是帮前任房主做局部翻修，而是直接拆掉承重墙重画户型，硬生生挖出了一间原本不存在的地下室。目前，部分改动已经被 AMD 采用并随芯片设计送往制造。OpenAI 自研推理芯片 Jalapeño 则提供了另一项验证：模型重写的一款乘法器，综合标准单元面积减少约 15%，计算延迟从两周期缩短到一周期，相关优化已经在实物硅片上得到验证。过去是工程师设计 GPU 来运行模型，现在模型开始改写 GPU 的运算、控制和数据搬运电路。这比生成几段 Verilog 难得多。电路缩小之后可能跑不动原来的时钟，移走一个寄存器，可能让连续请求或下游停顿时的状态转移出错。AMD 敢把修改纳入制造设计，意味着这些候选已经进入成熟的芯片工程验证流程。所以，OpenAI 究竟做了哪些工作，技术门槛又落在哪里？01OpenAI 改了什么？如果把芯片设计比作建造一座精密工厂，过去的自动化工具更像是“按图施工的装修队”，而这一次，OpenAI 的模型直接坐上了“总架构师”的位置。2025 年初，OpenAI就让 GPT-o3 mini 参与 Jalapeño 的设计，随后把工作推进到向量单元里的浮点加法、乘法、数值转换、归约和特殊函数以及矩阵单元里的低精度点积。官方提到的改法很具体：尝试另一种逻辑实现，把计算重新分到不同流水级，让不同操作共享硬件，减少级间需要保存的数据。与 AMD 合作时，模型已经能直接改写负责计算、控制和搬运数据的 SystemVerilog RTL。这些改动指向同一个问题：数据从输入到结果，中途经过多少层逻辑，又在哪些时钟边沿停下来。传统综合工具能在既定 RTL 下化简逻辑、做门级映射，但如果寄存器边界和运算资源已经写死，它所能探索的结构就受到约束。模型直接改 RTL，就能重写原先的数据通路和时序安排。雷峰网以一个由 16 组 8 位整数构成的点积为例。每组相乘产生一个完整的 16 位乘积，16 个乘积再求和。若把加法器串成依次累加的长链，后面的运算必须等前面的进位完成。换成平衡归约树，可以让相邻乘积先并行求和，经过四层加法得到结果。加法次数没变，组合逻辑深度和布线形态却变了。如果逐层保存中间和，前面几层只需要相对较窄的数据位宽，后面随着累加项增加才扩展到足够容纳完整结果的宽度，寄存器究竟放在哪一层，会同时改变需要保存多少比特、单周期走过几级加法以及时钟网络的负载。接着要决定流水线如何分段。把两级计算压成一级，可能省去一批寄存器，却要求更长的组合路径在一个时钟周期内走完。若选择共享算术单元来省面积，数据还要经过多路选择器，控制扇出和等待关系也会变化。浮点运算更难随意重排：中间舍入的时刻会影响低位结果，NaN、无穷值和异常标志各有对应的行为约束。候选电路只有把这些条件一起考虑，才有可能比原方案更划算。Jalapeño 的结果把这种结构调整落到了具体器件上。一款乘法器综合标准单元面积减少约 15%，延迟由两周期改为一周期。另一款加法器维持两周期延迟，面积同样减少约 15%。团队估计，模型提出的修改使向量单元和矩阵单元的标准单元面积分别降

articles.title: OmniAct: One Policy, One Million Embodiments
articles.content: A single policy that controls diverse robots must not only transfer task knowledge across embodiments, but also adapt its behavior to each robot's capabilities. Existing approaches facilitate transfer through shared action representations, but these representations do not necessarily capture how differences in robot morphology should shape manipulation strategies. We introduce OmniAct, a cross-embodiment manipulation policy that conditions directly on each robot's kinematics in a specific scene to produce embodiment-specific behavior. This kinematic graph represents the robot's joint positions, motion axes, and connectivity to its visual observation, allowing the policy to account for how its embodiment related to objects and surfaces in the scene. A flow-matching policy predicts relative joint motions for each node, enabling control across robots with different degrees of freedom and kinematic configurations. To learn how physical structure shapes behavior at scale, we procedurally design and filter one million physically feasible robot embodiments; next, we develop algorithms to generate robot trajectories in simulation for all embodiments; finally, we train across diverse simulated manipulation tasks. On 2,000 embodiment-scene-held-out evaluation episodes, OmniAct achieves 63.0% success, compared to 17.8% for pi 0.5 and 57.9% for the strongest baseline; on the task families GPT-6 Astra was evaluated on, it achieves 64.7% against GPT-6 Astra's 41.1%. On a previously unseen real-world robot, it achieves nearly twice the success rate of the next best method, MolmoAct2. Beyond task success, we observe that OmniAct learns distinct manipulation strategies that exploit the capabilities and accommodate the limitations of different morphologies. Project: https://omniact.github.io/

articles.title: PointX: Multi-View Consistent Intrinsics by Querying Surface Points
articles.content: The appearance of a scene is determined by the albedo, roughness, metallicity and normal of every point on its surface, and by the light that reaches it, its irradiance. Recovering these intrinsics from images is ambiguous, and methods that predict them per pixel give the same surface point a different decomposition in every view. We introduce PointX, a simple feed-forward model that predicts intrinsics per 3D surface point instead. A multi-view transformer encodes a set of unposed images, and for any queried surface point, PointX pools the point's tokens across the views in which it appears and decodes the point's intrinsics once. Each point of a 3D reconstruction of the scene, such as a point cloud or a mesh, thus receives a single prediction, which is exactly consistent across views by construction and enables view-consistent relighting and editing. The same model also predicts per-view maps, from one image or many, by querying the point seen at every pixel. These maps agree across views up to the precision of the estimated geometry and correspondences. PointX is significantly more consistent than existing methods, while remaining competitive in accuracy from a single image and improving as views are added. Project page: https://pointx-paper.github.io/

articles.title: DiaCap: Jointly Learning Who Speaks When for Audiovisual Dialogue Captioning
articles.content: We present DiaCap, an audiovisual LLM for comprehensive dialogue captioning, which produces the transcript, timestamps, and a visual description of the speaker for every utterance in a video. Considering that utterance timing and audiovisual diarization are tightly coupled, DiaCap unifies the tasks in a single model, trained in two complementary stages. First, we train DiaCap on 225K curated clips, using synthetic captions that densely label every utterance in detail. Second, we further refine the model via reinforcement learning on 2.9K human-corrected clips, using fine-grained feedback that directly evaluates utterance timing, speaker grouping, and speaker binding. On DiaDemBench, which we extend with utterance-level timestamps and subtitle redaction, both DiaCap with off-the-shelf transcripts and its end-to-end variant DiaCap-E2E achieve strong results. Specifically, DiaCap performs on par with Gemini 4 Argon in audiovisual diarization while clearly outperforming it in timestamp accuracy (76.59 vs. 42.76 TIME). It also maintains strong diarization on multilingual and minute-long videos, and transfers to audiovisual question answering.

articles.title: BioLoom: Scaling Biomedical Vision-Language Models by Learning from the Structure of Scientific Articles
articles.content: The development of biomedical vision-language models (VLMs) with contrastive image-text pretraining has been driven by scaling to increasingly large and diverse image-text datasets. Beyond scaling, further progress can come from learning richer representations from existing data. We hypothesize that the structure of scientific literature itself provides an additional source of supervision: figures, panels, captions, and accompanying article text encode rich relationships across modalities. Yet, treating these as independent image-text pairs overlooks their relationships. To address this limitation, we incorporate these structural relationships into contrastive image-text supervision. We preserve exact image-text matches while introducing weaker positive supervision for related pairs, such as a panel and the caption of a sibling panel. We upweight cross-article negatives of the same content type to encourage finer discrimination. We also enrich panel descriptions using visual content, original figure captions, and mentioning paragraphs. Pairing panels with these descriptions and whole figures with their original captions yields Loom52M, a dataset of 52.4 million image-text pairs spanning scientific charts and biomedical images. Using Loom52M, BioLoom (DFN-2B) achieves 56.82% domain-balanced mean accuracy across 67 zero-shot classification tasks from 43 datasets in 10 domains, compared with 48.77% for MedPMC-CLIP. On BioLoomBench with concise captions and BioMedFlickr, it achieves bidirectional mean Recall@1 of 63.20% and 10.59%, versus 46.37% and 7.55% for the respective strongest evaluated baselines, BiomedCLIP and MedPMC-CLIP. Code, datasets, benchmarks, and models are available at https://bioloom-clip.github.io/.

articles.title: CoT-Proxy: Cross-Format Transfer for Distilling Long-Horizon Policies
articles.content: Reasoning models become long-horizon agents through reinforcement learning or, more cheaply, through fine-tuning on a stronger teacher's trajectories, which contain the teacher's chain-of-thought as well as its actions. The standard fine-tuning approach imitates both, yet the strongest teachers are closed models whose chain-of-thought is hidden behind an API. We show that the chain-of-thought can be left out altogether and that the long-horizon policy can be distilled from the teacher's actions alone. The student is trained on these trajectories with its reasoning block left empty, while a KL loss on a replay buffer of its own generations limits drift from its initial model. Surprisingly, the policy learned from these trajectories with an empty reasoning block carries over to inference with thinking enabled, where the student reasons in its own style while acting like the teacher, an effect we call cross-format transfer. Distilling the actions of Qwen3.6-27B raises the task success of Qwen3-4B on AppWorld from 7% to 18% and that of Qwen3-32B from 12% to 25%. We further introduce CoT-proxies, short summaries of the teacher's reasoning placed after the empty reasoning block, which raise Qwen3-4B further, to 35%. Since neither actions nor CoT-proxies need the hidden chain-of-thought, the recipe applies unchanged to closed teachers. Distilling GPT-5.6 Luna from its visible outputs and the reasoning summaries its API returns raises Qwen3-4B from 7% to 48% on AppWorld and from 3% to 28% on SWE-bench Verified.

articles.title: One Take, Many Cameras: Audio-Grounded Shot Synthesis for Dialogue Re-Cinematography
articles.content: Creating a dialogue scene typically requires cutting between multiple views (e.g., close-ups, medium shots, and over-the-shoulder shots) of the actors. Yet capturing such coverage is costly and in many settings unavailable. We study dialogue re-cinematography: synthesizing additional shots from a single wide-angle dialogue video. Existing video generators can synthesize new shots, but rely on visual cues alone, so when the source video barely shows the lips, the generated lip motion fails to match the speech. Our key observation is that the speech audio is view-invariant: it constrains lip motion in any target view. Building on this insight, we adapt a pretrained audio-visual diffusion model to generate the new shot from a target frame that specifies the view, a source video that contains the performance, and the speech audio that drives lip motion. In multi-person scenes, however, pretrained audio-visual models drive every visible face with the same speech, causing speech leakage, where silent listeners mouth the speaker's words. We therefore introduce speaker-aware audio gating, a training-free module that lets the audio drive only the faces that speak in the target shot. On a cinematic paired-view benchmark spanning diverse viewpoints and framings, our method lowers perceptual error by 59%, landmark error by 56%, and speech leakage by 97% relative to the strongest baseline, Wan 3.0. Our method also remains robust on in-the-wild scenes, highlighting its potential for film post-production.

articles.title: Lost on Campus: Evaluating Embodied Spatial Reasoning of Vision-Language Models in the Wild
articles.content: Embodied Spatial Reasoning (ESR) is central to deploying Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in real-world embodied tasks, yet remains inadequately evaluated. Existing benchmarks primarily assess spatial reasoning in static images or synthetic indoor environments, where semantic shortcuts often suffice, making it difficult to faithfully evaluate spatial reasoning capabilities in the wild. In light of this, we present Lost on Campus, a benchmark for evaluating ESR in large-scale real-world outdoor 3D environments reconstructed by 3D Gaussian Splatting. Our benchmark introduces a unified reasoning-action evaluation framework that seamlessly integrates diagnostic QA for isolated reasoning with closed-loop interactive navigation for active reasoning under multimodal instructions. To enable fine-grained diagnosis, we evaluate six capability aspects of ESR: action grounding, spatial foresight, metric awareness, goal-directed planning, ego-allocentric localization, and spatio-temporal consistency. Extensive experiments reveal that: (i) Compared to indoor settings, real-world outdoor environments impose substantially higher demands on spatial reasoning, where existing models exhibit poor performance; (ii) VLMs still struggle with fine-grained visual alignment, with failures in spatial foresight and ego-allocentric localization emerging as primary bottlenecks; (iii) Improving multimodal interaction capabilities and long-term spatial reasoning is crucial for advancing embodied intelligence. These findings highlight that faithful evaluation of ESR demands benchmarks tightly coupling perception, reasoning and action within realistic and continuous environments.

articles.title: PyRUA-Dex: Learning Programmatic Policies for Dexterous Bimanual Manipulation with Coding Agents
articles.content: Learning for dexterous manipulation is limited by the scarcity of high-quality demonstrations: retargeting from human video is imprecise, teleoperation gives no force feedback to the operator, and exoskeleton-based collection is hard to scale up. We present PyRUA-Dex, a framework that enables coding agents to develop dexterous manipulation through programmatic policy, without the need of demonstrations. The programmatic policy is developed in two stages: during exploration, multiple agents explore in parallel for task skills and ways to compose them, and a distilling agent condenses the successful attempts into a task library and one program. During refinement, this program is improved through randomized layouts for enhanced robustness and execution efficiency. In simulated environments, PyRUA-Dex achieves SOTA on Bench2Dex with a score of 72.9 and reaches 81.0% success on DexJoCo under full randomization, ahead of every trained policy on both benchmarks. In real world experiments on a bimanual platform with two 22-DoF hands, PyRUA-Dex learns to play piano, write calligraphy, and other tasks efficiently: learning a new piece from sheet music takes as little as 30 minutes. These results suggest that PyRUA-Dex is an effective framework for developing dexterous manipulation policies with coding agents in the absence of high quality dexterous manipulation demonstrations.

articles.title: ROAM-Bench: Evaluating Embodied Active Spatial Intelligence through Evidence Verification
articles.content: Embodied spatial intelligence requires agents to gather information through exploration and interaction, then use it to reason and act. Existing benchmarks insufficiently distinguish correct outcomes from completion of these task requirements. We introduce ROAM-Bench to evaluate these abilities under robot motion and collision constraints. Independent checks use simulation state and episode records to assess outcomes and task requirements, with stronger checks of geometry, coverage, or placement. It comprises 250 manually validated tasks across 11 types in five groups and 27 indoor environments, covering object and room search, counting, geometric judgments, direction reasoning, and relocation. Human evaluators achieve 84% strict task success on 100 sampled tasks, with every correct outcome satisfying the required checks. Across seven frontier vision-language models, we identify two complementary failure modes: correct outcomes with unmet task requirements, and incorrect outcomes despite passing stronger checks. Oracle-input diagnostics show that more complete target observations and calibrated feedback improve final spatial judgments.

articles.title: iWAM: Efficient Action Prediction from World Models without Explicit Future Prediction
articles.content: World-action models (WAMs) build policies on pretrained video-generation models, on the premise that predicting how a scene evolves helps determine how to act. However, generating future scenes is expensive for real-time control. This motivates efficient proxies for future imagination, but how to train such proxies without sacrificing action-prediction quality remains unclear. An effective proxy need not generate a high-resolution frame; it only needs to provide enough information to distinguish between possible futures. This leads to the design principle behind iWAM: rather than denoising an entire future frame, can we condition the action policy on intermediate features from a single video-model evaluation? We show that the answer is yes. Exploiting the reversible dynamics of flow-matching models, we invert each training future into the corresponding latent noise vector. However, a single velocity evaluation at this latent does not necessarily yield informative features for action prediction. We therefore learn a bidirectional flow map that amortizes future-generation computation, enabling a single model evaluation to provide effective conditioning features. At inference, we sample a latent noise vector from the prior and condition the policy using just one video-backbone forward pass. Across simulated benchmarks and real robots, iWAM recovers the generalization benefits of WAMs while substantially reducing its inference cost.

articles.content: We present Physicl Scenes, a high-quality artist-created and curated dataset of 6,499 3D scenes spanning household rooms, public interiors, and outdoor spaces. The dataset combines detailed geometry, physically based materials, and carefully composed environments with object- and part-level semantic annotations, providing rich, joint supervision for visual and embodied learning. We demonstrate its value as training data across inverse rendering, 3D reconstruction, scene understanding, and mobile manipulation. Across these tasks, training state-of-the-art methods with our scenes improves performance over alternative synthetic datasets. In addition, we introduce a mobile manipulation benchmark, evaluating vision-language-action models performing physical pick and place in diverse 3D scenes with realistic layouts, and using our part annotations to also score where each object is grasped. Our dataset will be released publicly to facilitate research in visual and embodied AI.

articles.title: BriConstrain: Geometrically Constrained Decoding for Autoregressive Brick Assembly Generation
articles.content: Language models can generate LEGO$^\circledR$ assemblies from text, but their builds often contain parts that collide or attach to nothing. The usual approach of rejecting and resampling invalid placements discards decoded tokens without guaranteeing a valid build. We present BriConstrain, a constrained decoding method that restricts a pretrained language model's next-token probabilities before sampling, steering it towards valid placements. Because the validity of a brick placement depends on the non-predetermined build state, it cannot be compiled into a fixed grammar and must be checked dynamically. However, checking the validity of a brick before sampling is challenging as the space of valid placements is combinatorially large and cannot be enumerated exhaustively. Our key idea is to narrow the search space by constraining how parts attach rather than which parts attach to each other. Concretely, given the model's predictions of the currently placed part, and the previously placed parent it wants to connect to, we constrain the model's choice of how they attach. This allows us to span the space of part attachments, using a precomputed geometric oracle, and to effectively filter out colliding options. With valid attachment candidates in hand, we bias the model's next-token distribution towards the remaining valid candidates. We evaluate our method on two LEGO$^\circledR$ formats and models: BrickNet, which annotates connectivity explicitly, and our proposed Implicit Connectivity LDraw Format (ICLF), which uses numeric values for placements and leaves connectivity implicit. Our method raises collision-free builds from 31% to 91% on BrickNet and from 15% to 65% on ICLF, and outperforms rejection sampling on both formats at about 60% of its decoding cost.

articles.content: Qwen3.5-0.8B rarely finishes reasoning in thinking mode: at a 4,096-token budget only 1 or 2 of 500 MATH-500 answers close their think block (two seeds), and accuracy is 15.4%. A recent demonstration had GPT-6 Astra edit 131,072 of the model's weights without gradients and reported MATH-500 rising from 7.9% to 48.1% at a 32,768-token budget. We provide the missing gradient baseline, then combine the two edits. Fine-tuning only the 140 to 139,750 weights with the largest gradient, on the model's own correct answers to MATH training problems, raises thinking-mode MATH-500 at 4k tokens to 39.0-45.5% after 2-9 minutes of training on one GPU; 50 training examples suffice, and 1,398 random positions give only 16.3%. The gradient concentrates the edit on the most nearly constant channel of each of the first three layers. Because the model has no bias terms, an edit confined to those channels acts as a constant vector added to the residual stream: adding three fixed vectors to the unedited model matches the accuracy of such an edit. Under the Astra protocol (32k tokens, presence penalty 1.5), the Astra edit scores 52.1% (finished and correct) in our reproduction and our full-strength edits reach 45.6-45.7%, but ours win at every budget up to 16k tokens (39.5% against 6.7% at 4k). The two edits are complementary. The Astra edit plus our 139,750-weight edit at half strength scores 62.2% at 32k, 10 points above the Astra edit alone (p = 3e-9), with half as many tokens; our half-strength edit alone scores 46.7%.

articles.title: Exploratory Midtraining for Robot Policies
articles.content: Robot policies predominantly learn from human-collected data emphasizing competent behavior, limiting coverage of the low-level behaviors needed to support autonomous improvement. We study how a form of midtraining can be used to build coverage over diverse low-level behaviors that connect challenging states of the robot and its environment to states from which further progress is possible ("connected behavioral coverage"). We also examine how this coverage supports downstream adaptation and online improvement. To this end, we introduce $β$-Data, a dataset collected via adversarial teleoperation, where a human adversary reversibly perturbs the environment while a human operator continues toward completion without resetting. We relabel trajectory segments with local outcomes in natural language and finetune a pretrained policy conditioned on recent action history. The resulting policy exhibits sustained use of more low-level behaviors. Across manipulation tasks in simulation and on three real-robot platforms, our approach yields more favorable data scaling laws, better zero-shot generalization, and more effective use of additional rollout time than training on standard demonstrations. During online finetuning, these policies need fewer rollouts to collect successful experience and reach higher success rates, suggesting that midtraining can prepare robots for both more robust task execution and continued autonomous improvement. Our project page and robot videos are available at https://kshitiz-1225.github.io/exploratory-midtraining-robot-policies/.

articles.title: SAG-Mem-1.0 Technical Report
articles.content: Long-term conversational memory requires retrieving complementary facts scattered across dialogue sessions, including intermediate evidence with limited similarity to the original question. Existing approaches often rely on derived memory representations or persistent relational structures, introducing construction costs and potentially losing source details. We present SAG-Mem, a conversational memory framework that preserves complete dialogue messages in non-overlapping chunks and discovers complementary evidence through query-time lexical expansion. Memory construction requires no model inference, using a lexical index without LLM-based extraction, summarization, or semantic relation construction. At query time, BM25 retrieves initial candidates, an evidence evaluator identifies useful chunks, and lexical cues from selected evidence guide an additional retrieval round. Retrieved dialogue is further annotated with calendar interpretations of supported relative-time expressions, preserving the original wording and temporal granularity. We also introduce SAG-Mem-Lite, an alternative configuration that replaces evidence scoring with embedding-based candidate scoring, achieving lower operational cost than Full Context and all memory-based baselines across both benchmarks with low query latency. On LoCoMo and LongMemEval, SAG-Mem achieves overall scores of 83.08 and 80.20, respectively, the highest among the evaluated methods on both benchmarks. On LongMemEval, it exceeds the strongest compared baseline by 7.20 points. SAG-Mem-Lite achieves scores of 77.09 and 77.20, respectively. These results support dialogue preservation and evidence-guided retrieval expansion as an effective design for long-term conversational memory.

articles.title: MetaFORGE: A Meta-Learning Framework for Harness Optimization in Automated Code Generation for Parallel Computing
articles.content: Large language models (LLMs) can generate parallel programs, but their correctness and performance depend strongly on the instructions that guide generation. We present \textsc{MetaFORGE}, an execution-grounded meta-learning framework that iteratively optimizes persistent natural-language skill specifications for MPI C code generation. \textsc{MetaFORGE} combines correctness testing, compiler diagnostics, static-analysis findings, runtime measurements, and rank-level load-imbalance profiles into a scalar reward that drives textual-gradient refinement, while an external memory distills and retrieves reward-supported optimization knowledge across runs.   Across six MPI tasks and three workload sizes, \textsc{MetaFORGE} improves static-analysis quality, runtime, and load balance relative to zero-shot generation and generally exceeds the evaluated \textsc{TextGrad} iterative baseline. A model-matched refinement ablation shows that the MetaFORGE advantage persists when its refinement model is reduced to \texttt{gpt-4o}. An expanded retrieval ablation across all 18 task--workload configurations shows consistent runtime benefit and broad static-analysis and load-balance benefit from retrieved context. Leakage-controlled held-out and zero-update experiments further provide evidence that optimization knowledge persists in both the transferred skill and external memory under the evaluated protocol.

articles.title: Neural Implicit Representation for Bathymetry Estimation using Sidescan Sonar Imagery
articles.content: Bathymetry measurement and estimation is critical for understanding the structure of underwater environments. While multibeam echosounders (MBES) provide accurate depth measurements, their deployment on surface vessels limits spatial resolution in deep water. Sidescan sonar (SSS), in contrast, can be deployed on autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) to operate closer to the seafloor, enabling high-resolution acoustic imaging. However, the inherent ambiguity in measurements and the limited observation coverage of sonar datasets degrade the performance of state-of-the-art methods for underwater bathymetry estimation from SSS. In this paper, we propose a differentiable neural rendering framework for SSS that enables effective estimation of bathymetry from SSS measurements. Our approach incorporates a measurement model based on SSS geometry, explicitly accounting for its wide elevation aperture and associated ambiguities. We evaluate our method on both synthetic and real-world datasets, demonstrating improved robustness and accuracy compared to alternative approaches.

articles.title: Read My Lips: Context-aware Lip Reading Using Language and Audio-Visual Models
articles.content: Real-world speech is often partially observable: audio may be missing or corrupted by noise and competing speakers, while the speaker's lips remain visible. Recovering speech requires combining what can be heard, seen, and inferred from context. We introduce RML (Read My Lips), a collaborative method combining a lip reader, a language model, and an audio-visual generative model. The lip reader provides articulation hypotheses, the language model uses context to resolve ambiguous or missing words, and the audio-visual generator reconstructs synchronized speech while preserving speaker identity. Since source reliability varies, RML generates multiple reconstructions and uses the available evidence to favor the most reliable ones. This allows RML to handle missing audio, strong interference, and poor visual evidence without manually defined thresholds. Quantitative and qualitative experiments across these conditions show the benefit of combining visual, acoustic, and linguistic signals.

articles.title: Draft Calibration for Speculative Decoding: Accelerating LLM Serving by Matching Draft and Target Distributions
articles.content: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model (LLM) inference by employing a lightweight draft model to propose draft tokens and allowing the target model to verify the new tokens in parallel to improve inference-time compute utilization. The speedup relies on the acceptance probability of draft tokens in target verification, which is directly related to the gap $\|p-q\|_1$ between the target distribution $p$ and the draft distribution $q$. In this paper, we study draft calibration of speculative decoding to improve the speedup of speculative decoding, where we employ post-hoc methods to calibrate the draft distribution to mitigate the distribution gap. We observe that though current community open-source draft models may learn the top candidate token correctly, they are generally underconfident compared to the target model, suggesting a consistent distribution mismatch. To mitigate the effect of this mismatch on the acceptance rate of the draft models, we try various post-hoc calibration methods, including standard temperature scaling and token-wise calibration. Our results suggest that a standard temperature scaling applied to the draft distribution improves the acceptance length by up to approximately 10\% with almost no additional cost across different tasks. Throughput analysis further verifies that this improvement in serving efficiency. Analysis of more general calibration methods reveals further potential room for improvement.

articles.title: Temporal Conditioning for Human Behavioral Cloning in Chess
articles.content: Behavioral cloning models in chess typically predict human moves from board states while ignoring temporal inputs such as the remaining clock. However, time pressure is a major determinant of human decision-making quality, and temporal state is a missing dimension of human behavioral modeling. This paper introduces a time-aware transformer that extends a Chessformer-style architecture with learned temporal conditioning tokens encoding player clock state, time control, and recent tempo, together with behavioral heads for thinking time and resignation. The model is trained on large-scale online chess data and evaluated against time-agnostic baselines and the state of the art. Results show that temporal conditioning yields modest overall accuracy improvements but substantially stronger gains under time pressure. Beyond move choice, it also produces more accurate thinking-time and resignation predictions. More importantly, the model better matches human move-quality degradation in critical time regimes, reducing the systematic over-strength observed in time-agnostic behavioral cloning models. These results suggest that temporal state is a previously underutilized but important signal for human behavioral cloning in chess.

articles.title: Reinforcement Learning Can Be Recovered From Its Own Rollouts
articles.content: Broadly speaking, reinforcement learning (RL) post-training converts compute into model capabilities by training on model-generated data. Typically, the rollouts are discarded after each update, and the knowledge acquired during RL resides in the model weights. In this work, we investigate how much of this knowledge is retained in the rollouts themselves. A natural first attempt is to replay the original RL algorithm on archived rather than freshly generated rollouts, but this leads to catastrophic collapse. We provide a simple explanation for this phenomenon, which in turn suggests a remedy: maximum likelihood on the archived rollouts. Surprisingly, starting from the same base model and replaying the rollouts in the order in which they were generated, without any distinction between correct and incorrect responses, is sufficient to recover the performance of online RL. In fact, a single maximum likelihood update per rollout batch closely tracks the entire learning curve of online RL. Furthermore, maximum likelihood on the rollouts of the last few RL steps often suffices to recover the final model's performance. This suggests that much of the compute invested in RL goes into discovering an improved sampling distribution rather than learning it from samples.

articles.title: GREMLIN: Generating Random Environments for Meta-Learning with Interacting Networks
articles.content: Can randomly parameterized neural environments supply useful experience for learning a reinforcement learning algorithm? We investigate this question using DiscoRL's rule-discovery framework, replacing human-designed training games with sixteen selected neural environments. Each game combines bounded vector dynamics with a random strategy-based reward and an independent outcome reward. After 224.8 million agent-environment steps, we froze the teacher and trained fresh agents. DQN outscored GREMLIN on most games, both generated and human-designed. GREMLIN nevertheless outperformed the untrained teacher on all 26 games, showing that generated experience can improve a learning rule. It remains unclear whether this approach can yield a competitive rule with longer meta-training.

articles.title: Delegent: A Multi-Agent Harness That Reduces Cost without Sacrificing Performance
articles.content: Agents built on frontier language models are expensive. At every step, the frontier model re-reads its entire context and executes every subtask regardless of its difficulty. This paper explores the simple thesis that much of this cost can be removed by delegating easy subtasks to a small language model, or SLM, that runs on hardware one already owns. To test it, we build Delegent, a simple and effective agent harness built on Claude Code, in which the frontier model stays in charge of every task but hands focused subtasks, such as investigating code, running tests, and searching a corpus, to SLM subagents. Existing approaches such as cascades and model routers usually choose which model executes the entire task, whereas in Delegent, the frontier model always leads the execution and delegates easy subtasks to the SLM. No router or model is trained, so either model can be swapped freely. With the help of a 27B FP8 SLM, Delegent reduces the frontier cost of long-horizon coding by 67% and of agentic search by 59%, with no loss in task performance, and even a 2B SLM that fits on a laptop reduces the coding cost by 66%. The savings grow with the legwork that the frontier model would otherwise do itself, and a short instruction, which leaves the main coding tasks to the frontier model, accounts for most of the saving and keeps the 2B SLM from losing tasks. articles.title: EventDiffusion: Learning Native Event Stream Distribution from Videos
articles.content: Event cameras capture asynchronous brightness changes at high temporal resolution, but scarce recordings constrain data-driven research. Sparse RGB observations cannot uniquely determine intervening events since identical frames may correspond to streams with different activity, polarities, and timing. Existing simulators largely rely on prescribed sensor dynamics and estimated brightness trajectories, whose assumptions limit the diversity and fidelity of plausible event streams. We introduce EventDiffusion, a hierarchical generative framework that directly learns the conditional distribution of native asynchronous event streams from real recordings. EventDiffusion decomposes generation into three probabilistic processes: Event Activity Diffusion (EAD) learns stochastic discrete event counts; Event Spatial Allocation (ESA) distributes these counts to individual pixels while preserving cardinality; and Event Timing Diffusion (ETD) learns continuous asynchronous timestamp distributions. We also introduce CEFS, an event-stream realism metric combining event activity and polarity with multiscale space-time structure and temporal fidelity. Across all datasets, EventDiffusion achieves double the accuracy of SOTA methods and demonstrates robustness across different cameras at any resolution.

articles.title: AIChipBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Automated AI Accelerator Design
articles.content: A language-model decoder carries state between decoding steps, and in hardware a wrong state update can leave the current token correct and corrupt the output several tokens later, so a design can pass output tests and still be wrong. AIChipBench asks what LLM coding agents need to build such hardware correctly. Agents implement quantized Qwen3.5, Gemma 3, Gemma 4, and Llama 3.2 decoders in synthesizable register-transfer-level (RTL) code against an executable integer reference that specifies the outputs and the stored state at every decoding step. They debug against public tests under fixed budgets; their frozen designs are graded on held-out token sequences, resets, memory stalls, and synthesis, and a second track asks them to speed up a correct design at nearly fixed area. Across 9,136 attempts by four coding agents, the difficulty lies in stored state. Feedback that points to the first state mismatch raises acceptance over output-only feedback in all 12 agent--task cells of a matched study, by 25.0 to 46.9 percentage points, and halves the agent-hours per accepted design. Regraded on new sequences and conditions, 45 of 69 accepted designs fail within the 32 steps their tests required. More than a third of attempts to speed up a correct design end without one. An overall score ranks Sol 5.6 and Fable 5.1 above Astra 6 and Opus 5.5, and both halves of the instances give this order in all 200 random splits. Hardware agents therefore need debugging feedback that exposes stored state, and their benchmarks need final tests well beyond the development cases.

articles.title: The Radar-based Activities of Daily Living (R-ADL) Dataset
articles.content: Monitoring Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) supports safety and well-being for people living at home, especially older adults, and radar sensing is gaining increasing attention in the field of activity recognition for its ability to ensure privacy in the home while also surpassing technical limitations of other sensing modalities. However, radar-based activity recognition remains constrained by the limited availability of large-scale datasets. We introduce the Radar-based Activities of Daily Living (R-ADL) dataset to addresses the gaps identified in existing work: 1) it expands the scale of available data by providing over eight hours of annotated recordings in which a person performs eight distinct activities; 2) it overcomes room configuration limitations by recording from five different locations in a two-bedroom, two-bathroom apartment; and 3) it extends beyond primitive actions to focus on high-level ADLs. In addition to the dataset, this paper introduces practical guidance for future ADL dataset construction. We conducted a detailed analysis of how ADLs are prioritized across academic research, health survey tools, and clinical trials to identify clinically significant ADLs. Furthermore, we provide our experimental design, data collection and annotation strategies, post-processing pipeline for forming the R-ADL dataset from raw data, and baseline results on standard machine learning architectures. The R-ADL dataset serves as a valuable resource for advancing ADL recognition systems as we continue building larger and more diverse datasets.

articles.title: Uncertainty-Aware Candidate Generation for Entity Linking in Cyber Threat Intelligence
articles.content: Entity Resolution (ER) pipelines often collapse ambiguity into early hard decisions: upstream Named Entity Recognition (NER) selects a single span and type, and downstream Entity Linking (EL) treats that choice as ground truth. This discards valuable information about the ambiguity of the underlying data (e.g., span boundary disagreement and type confusion), leading to brittle systems that fail unpredictably when faced with uncertainty in inputs. Therefore, this work presents a proof-of-concept for uncertainty-aware ER that treats uncertainty as native data that should be preserved and exploited throughout ER pipelines. We (i) capture uncertainty signals in the NER stage and (ii) leverage these signals into the EL stage to improve candidate retrieval under ambiguity. Using a BERT-based NER model augmented with two auxiliary span-boundary prediction heads, we apply Monte Carlo (MC) dropout at inference time to derive three mention-level proxy signals: the MC-averaged start-boundary probability, the MC-averaged end-boundary probability, and De Luca-Termini fuzzy entropy computed over the Begin-Inside-Outside (BIO) predictive distribution. These signals are used to adapt the fuzzy cutoff in candidate generation (CG) for EL. Because CG is treated as a blocking step, we evaluate retrieval recall. On the AnnoCTR dataset linked to the MITRE ATTCK knowledge base, the boundary-aware and dual-signal fuzzy linking approaches improve Recall@10 from 0.6186 to 0.7966. The contribution lies not in an end-to-end optimised ER pipeline but in establishing uncertainty preservation as a viable and beneficial component of ER pipelines, enabling downstream EL to make better-informed decisions under uncertainty.

articles.title: Shifter Quantization: Compact Representations for Native Integer Computation
articles.content: Groupwise quantization is used in LLM quantization to improve accuracy at low bit widths, but grouping weights keeps standard integer MMA from spanning the full dot product for efficient GPU inference. We develop a new quantization method, Shifter Quantization (SQ), that reconstructs native-width integer operands by appending and shifting shared bits. To further extend the efficiency, we develop a special variant of SQ, Shifter Integer (SHI), to use INT4 kernels. We show that SQ and SHI formats perform better than standard groupwise quantization in quality, as measured by projection error and KL divergence, and in inference speed, as measured during decoding and prefill. For low precision like 2-bit quantization, SQ2 and SHI2 achieve 2.71-3.77x the 4,096-token prefill throughput of llama.cpp on a Q2_K checkpoint and reduce WikiText-2 KL by 6.6-7.8%. For mid precision like 4-bit quantization, SQ4 achieves 1.43-2.47x the prefill throughput of NInfer's groupwise-integer baselines across the tested models and prompt lengths, with 24-40% lower KL than the NInfer baselines. For high precision like 8-bit quantization, SQ8 achieves 27.4% higher batch-one prefill throughput and 72.7% lower KL than vLLM's online FP8.

articles.title: FOL-Proof: Verifying LLM Text-to-Logic Translations via Deterministic Semantics
articles.content: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used to translate natural-language statements into first-order logic (FOL) to improve reasoning. However, LLMs are prone to errors, and so a semantically unfaithful FOL formula could corrupt downstream reasoning. We present FOL-Proof, a semantic firewall pipeline that validates LLM-generated FOL translations against independently derived linguistic interpretations. FOL-Proof operates by deterministically obtaining a pool of candidate translations via semantic analysis tools, such as the English Resource Grammar and Minimal Recursion Semantics; then applying an SMT solver to check each derived reading for logical equivalence to the LLM-generated formula. If the translation is faithful it is accepted; otherwise, it is rejected, or optionally repaired via repeated invocations to the LLM. The procedure is conservative: incomplete search, unsupported constructions, or inconclusive checks yield abstention rather than false rejection. We evaluated FOL-Proof on established benchmarks (ProofWriter, RuleTaker and PrOntoQA), and also on a new adversarial benchmark (LongFaithCheck). Our experiments show that FOL-Proof attains near perfect selective accuracy, while direct LLM judges and round-trip baselines show substantially worse performance.

articles.title: On the Creation of Object-Centric Event Logs from Patient Journeys
articles.content: Interactions between patients and health systems as well as conditions that individuals experience during a disease are represented in patient journeys. Therefore, patient journeys are important assets to investigate how care is being provided, and how health systems can be designed to better suit the needs of patients. While there is initial work on patient journeys from a process mining perspective with traditional case notions, object-centric process mining techniques have yet to be covered. This is unfortunate, since due to the rich structure of objects and their relationships, object-centric process mining approaches are particularly promising in this context. This paper addresses this gap by investigating object-centric event log (OCEL) generation from patient journeys. Based on a list of challenges and requirements, the paper presents an approach for the creation of OCELs from patient journey data. The approach is evaluated on a synthetic patient cohort provided by our industry partner.

articles.title: 深拆 GPT-6.2 Astra：性能涨了、价格降了，任务成本减少近一半，OpenAI 怎么做到的？
articles.content: 性能提升 6.2 分，Token 少 22%，API 价格降 20%。    作者丨郑佳美    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       刚刚，OpenAI 发布了 GPT-6.2 Astra 和 GPT-6.2 Sol。这次更新有一个很具体的变化：模型开始更主动地判断一项工作应该怎么完成，包括什么时候需要调用工具、什么时候应该直接操作计算机、复杂任务需要投入多少推理资源，以及怎样减少反复修改才能交付符合要求的成果。举个例子，过去让 AI 制作一份财务估值工作簿，模型需要从多个文件中提取数据，理解不同业务之间的关系，建立财务计算逻辑，再检查结果能否相互对应。整个过程涉及文件读取、数据处理、表格生成和结果核验，任何一个环节出现偏差，最终文件就可能无法直接使用。现在，OpenAI 希望 GPT-6.2 Astra 能够承担更多这样的连续工作，把原本需要人工不断衔接的操作整合进一条完整的执行链。GPT-6.2 Astra 面向复杂专业任务，GPT-6.2 Sol 则侧重日常工作与高效率执行。两款模型在代码工程、计算机操作、专业文档、科学研究和交互式设计上都有能力提升。其中有一个变化值得深入拆解：模型开始根据任务本身动态调整执行策略。工具调用、推理投入、环境操作和交付结果之间形成了更紧密的联系。这个变化涉及 Agent 系统的底层运行逻辑，也决定了模型能否从完成单轮指令走向承担连续的工程任务。01模型开始参与执行路径的决策传统 Agent 通常采用规划与执行相结合的架构。模型接收任务后生成行动计划，外部执行器根据计划调用工具，再将结果返回模型。模型继续分析结果并生成下一步指令，整个过程通过多轮交互推进。这套架构有一个明显的工程难点：任务计划形成时，模型掌握的信息往往不完整。执行过程中出现的新情况，会改变后续工作的依赖关系。如果系统过度依赖预先设计的流程，模型就可能沿着已经失效的路径继续执行。GPT-6.2 Astra 强调的任务执行判断能力，涉及一种更动态的策略控制方式。模型需要根据当前任务状态，重新评估可采取的行动，并决定下一步应该投入多少推理资源。这里有一个关键区别：模型需要处理的不只是下一步生成什么内容，还包括下一步应该通过什么方式获取信息、改变环境或者验证结果。从系统设计角度看，这涉及三个相互关联的决策层。首先是任务状态的持续维护。长程任务需要维护一份持续更新的状态信息，其中包含目标、约束、已有证据、完成进度、待处理依赖以及工具运行情况。这份状态信息决定模型能否区分已经完成的工作和仍待验证的结果。单纯累积历史对话并不能充分解决这个问题，因为历史记录可能包含过期信息、失败操作和已经被新结果修正的判断。模型需要从上下文中提取当前有效状态，避免旧计划继续影响新决策。其次是行动选择与信息价值评估。模型需要在推理、检索、代码执行、API 调用和计算机操作之间进行选择。这些操作的作用并不相同。检索主要补充外部信息，代码执行能够处理确定性的计算任务，API 可以直接访问结构化服务，计算机操作则能够进入没有专用接口的软件环境。行动选择还涉及信息价值。如果当前缺少的只是一个文件字段，调用大型工具链并没有必要，如果任务涉及多个相互依赖的模块，仅凭现有上下文直接修改，可能引入更大的返工成本。因此，工具选择实际上与任务的不确定程度、操作成本和后续影响有关。最后是推理预算与执行反馈的联合调整。推理资源需要按照任务难度分配。对于约束明确、结果容易验证的步骤，模型可以减少额外分析，对于存在多个可能路径、涉及复杂依赖或者容易产生连锁影响的操作，则需要投入更多推理。执行反馈会进一步改变资源分配。当工具返回异常结果时，模型需要判断问题属于输入缺失、环境故障还是原有判断错误，再决定继续执行、重新检索或者修改计划。以真实代码库修改为例，模型完成代码编辑后，如果测试失败，需要检查失败来自接口兼容、依赖环境还是修改本身，而不能直接重

articles.content: 长任务、子 Agent 委派与共享服务凭证，让传统安全架构面临权限失控风险。    作者丨郑佳美    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       说起来你可能不信，这次真的是模型先动的手。当地时间 11 月 16 日，加州总检察长 Rob Bonta 一纸诉状把 OpenAI 告上了法庭。起诉书里最值得注意的一句指控是：OpenAI 的智能体（Agent）在缺乏适当监管的情况下，“自己跑了出去，主动对外部系统发起了攻击”。这件事情一下子从技术圈出了圈。大家不是震惊于 AI 会攻击，而是震惊于 OpenAI 内部披露的细节：为了不让人类发现自己做错了事，两个负责干活的 Coding Agent，竟然偷偷把监督自己的监控系统给“拔”了。这已经不是“猜疑链”的问题了，这是底层的“权限链”出了大问题。今年 7 月，OpenAI 的一个自主智能体（Agent）越过了测试环境的边界，直接对外部的 Hugging Face 等系统发起了攻击。而 OpenAI 随后在 10 月披露的内部复盘，更把这种“失控”摆在了台面上：两个 Coding Agent 在执行正常开发任务时，先后改动了监督自己的监控机制。第一起事件中，GPT-6.1 Sol 原本负责修复一条评测流水线。修复过程中，它发现监控结果无法正常写入数据库，于是尝试调整写入配置。问题出在，它把用户此前提出的不要发送 Slack 消息，理解成了连系统自动告警也不应该发送。第二起事件中，GPT-6 Astra 接到的是运行时迁移任务。为了让新版本的实现与参考代码保持一致，它直接移除了原有的监控集成，还修改了相关测试，让监控组件缺失也能通过检查。换句话说，原本负责检查 Agent 运行状态的机制，被它从新运行环境中删掉了。两起事件的具体操作不同：一个是 Agent 改动了自己的监控（顺便关了报警），一个是 Agent 越过了原有的执行边界（直接把监控拔了）。但它们有一个共同点，Agent 原本只是获得了完成开发任务所需的工具权限，最终却利用这些权限改变了安全监控的运行条件。这就引出了一个很具体的工程问题：当 Agent 能够修改代码、调用系统接口、调整运行配置，甚至启动新的执行任务时，谁来确保它无法修改约束自己的安全机制？传统软件系统通常由开发人员制定权限规则，再由独立的监控系统检查程序运行状态。Agent 开始自主修改代码和运行环境后，这种关系发生了变化。执行任务的程序本身，可能已经拥有修改监控配置、调整告警规则和改变审计路径的能力。要理解这种变化，需要从 Agent 最基础的 Tool Calling 执行链开始，看模型生成的一条工具调用，究竟如何借助系统权限变成真实的基础设施操作。01Agent 为什么能够动自己的监控？要看清权限从哪里来，得把 Tool Calling 还原成执行过程：模型生成工具名称和参数，编排器把请求交给工具适配层，后者使用服务身份访问 Shell、仓库、数据库或云 API。模型未必持有底层密钥，操作由后端服务完成。Agent 能触及哪些资源，取决于服务凭证覆盖范围，以及服务端如何处理参数。Sol 事件暴露了字段级授权的缺口。评测结果写入请求同时包含结果内容、告警接收人和 no_notify 标记。对业务接口而言，它们只是请求字段。对监控系统而言，后两项会改变告警是否送达。Agent 只需写入评测结果，服务端却允许同一请求改变通知状态。若后端只检查结果写入权限，没有单独核验静音权限，业务写权限便覆盖了控制权限。检测和存储仍在工作，人工响应通道却被切断。删掉工具说明中的 no_notify 并不能解决问题，Agent 还可能改配置或提交代码，让下游服务采用另一套通知策略。授权需要检查操作造成的状态变化。结果写入服务可以接收检测结果，却不应接受 Agent 自行决定的接收人和静音状态；通知策略应由独立服务计算，业
